On behalf of the children, staff and governors I would like to warmly welcome you to our Maple Ridge School website.
I am very proud to be the Headteacher here, where we work together to secure the most relevant education for all, and always believe that anything is possible!
Maple Ridge School is a Primary Special School for children with Moderate Learning Difficulties, many of our children also have a diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder and/or Severe Learning Difficulties. All of our children have an Education Health & Care Plan, and we work closely with numerous professionals to ensure that we provide the appropriate provision for each individual child.
We update the website regularly, with calendar dates for parents, class/whole school newsletters, and any updates explaining what's going on in school. Each class has their own page, which can be found by visiting the class pages section of our website.
Welcome to our school
I hope that you find the site interesting, useful and informative, as well as providing up-to-date information for parents, pupils and the wider community.
If you require more information please do not hesitate to contact the school on 01256 323639 or email enquiries@mapleridge.hants.sch.uk.
If you call the school, one of our friendly office staff will be more than happy to help you in any way they can.

Welcome to Maple Ridge School
Working together to secure the most relevant education for all and believing anything is possible
At Maple Ridge School, we aim to make a difference to all of our pupils and their families by ensuring that children are happy, feel safe and enjoy their school experience.
We provide an individually tailored education to prepare them for life ahead, by enabling children to have the confidence and self-esteem to be ready to learn. We focus on developing self-awareness, social interaction and communication skills.
Our vision is to provide all children with the opportunity to reach their potential and be as independent as possible, equipped with the necessary skills to be positively included in the local community and the wider society.
Visions and Values
At Maple Ridge we aim to:
Provide opportunities for the staff to further develop their skills and expertise
Reward achievement, however small
Teach children to reflect on their own actions and successes
Be role models in the way in which we behave towards each other
Be approachable and accessible to children and their parents
Maintain regular contact with parents and keep them informed of their child’s progress
Ensure effective teamwork within school and effective partnerships within the community
Be a centre of expertise providing support to the wider community
We aim to provide a curriculum that will:
Enable pupils to interact and communicate with a wide range of people, teaching communication support systems where necessary
Encourage pupils to apply their learning into real life situations
Increase pupils' awareness and understanding of their environment and the world
Comprise suitably differentiated and achievable work activities
Enable pupils to express preferences, communicate needs appropriately, make choices and make decisions

Joining and Leaving Maple Ridge
Here we provide some transition information to parents of children who have had a place confirmed by SEN for their child to start at Maple Ridge. We have created this information page for new parents, and will update this with more information once we have it.
A confirmed place means that you have had a formal offer letter from Hampshire County Council and you have returned this offer letter to confirm your acceptance of the place. Hampshire County Council have then informed Maple Ridge School of your acceptance of the place and sent the school the final EHCP paperwork.
Joining our School
What happens once a place has been confirmed?
Closer to the time your child is due to start Maple Ridge, a member of staff will be in contact with both parents and your child’s current school/pre-school setting to discuss all the information we might need about your child and answer any questions you may have.
The majority of children starting Maple Ridge School will start at the beginning of the academic year (September).
Usually, towards the end of June or beginning of July, a parent information meeting is held, which the parents of all children with a confirmed place receive an invitation for.
We will try and provide you with any paperwork you need to fill out and information before this meeting, so that you have time to read it and can then ask questions.
All transition support can be adapted to meet your child’s need, we pride ourselves on supporting children and families and aim to make this as smooth a process as possible for everyone.
When will we tell you what class your child is in and who the teacher will be?
We do not usually tell any pupils or parents what classes children are in until the last week of the school term. Due to a number of factors, including the intake of new children, we are often still finalising classes in June and early July and will only let people know what class groups will be once we are certain they are finalised to avoid any confusion or unnecessary changes.
What about children who have already been to school?
For children who have already been to school (usually those starting Maple Ridge in year 1 or above), a visit may be arranged to see your child in their current school. Sometimes pupils will be invited for some Stay and Play sessions, which is an opportunity for your child to come into school and play in our community room or in an outside space, meeting some other new children and some of the staff. Following this, you will be provided with information about start dates and times. Most children, who have already been to school, start full time.
What about children who have not yet started school (usually joining in Year R)?
In September your child will most likely have a part-time start. In the first week of term they will usually come into school for half days, in the morning or afternoon. On the second week your child will attend school full-time.
What if my child is transitioning mid-year?
For children transitioning into Maple Ridge part way through the school year, an individual transition programme will be agreed with parents.
Leaving Our School

Our Staff
At Maple Ridge pupils are placed in one of 10 classes according to their age, and each class is named after a tree.
The average class size is 10 pupils and there are generally 3 or 4 adults in each class, including the class teacher.
The classes are split into 3 'Teams' and they work in their teams for a multitude of topics, school performances and school trips.

Governors
School Governors have responsibility for raising school standards through their three key roles of setting strategic direction, ensuring accountability, and monitoring and evaluating school performance.
You can find out more about the governors' role and volunteering opportunities by visiting the Hampshire County Council Website.

Support for Parents and Children
Maple Ridge School has been accredited by the Hampshire Local Authority to provide an outreach service to mainstream schools in Basingstoke and Deane.
Outreach Service
To provide our local mainstream schools with specialist support to enable them to best meet the needs of their children/young people with SEND.
To support children/young people to thrive and fulfil their full potential within a mainstream setting.
To provide high-quality training.
The Outreach Team offer a warm and friendly referral-based service and can provide the following areas of support:
Liaison with SENCos, teachers and school staff to offer advice and strategies.
A planned programme of support.
Setting up the learning environment.
Curriculum differentiation.
We also run training for school staff throughout the year. Training schedules will be distributed to all SENCOs at the start of the school year. Please email the Outreach team if you wish to receive another copy.
A referral form must be filled out (see link below).
An initial consultation is required to ascertain the best way to support your needs.
Verbal parental consent is required before we can visit a child in school.
Staff will need to be released from their timetable to receive feedback and support from the outreach team on the day of their visit.
Evidence must be shown that recommendations have been implemented between each visit.
School staff in receipt of outreach support are invited to attend a training session at Maple Ridge. This will include topics such as understanding visuals, TEACCH approach, engagement curriculum, sensory processing and emotional regulation.
Hampshire County Council will also require you to fill out an evaluation sheet after receiving outreach support.
The outreach service does not interact with parents, it’s the school’s responsibility to store and share information provided by the outreach team with parents.
We are unable to work with a child currently receiving support from Portage, Helen Tongue, PBS or where SEMH is the main area of need.
Our resource library is open fortnightly, to all staff engaging in our outreach service. There is an annual fee of £20.00 which will go towards maintenance of equipment.
Staff are encouraged to borrow a wide variety of resources that include cause and effect toys, puzzles, games, workstation tasks and equipment for the use of interventions such as intensive interactions and identi-play.
For further information, you can contact us via email.
The Outreach Team: outreach@mapleridge.hants.sch.uk
Home / School Support
We have a very successful Home/School Service offering different levels of support to families.
SHIP (School Home Integrated Partnership) is part of the school’s Home/ School Service.
The aim is to support parents/carers and families of youngsters who have learning difficulties and behaviours that can be hard to manage and affect family life. This may include difficulties such as toileting, eating or sleep issues or challenging behaviour within the family. Our home school co-ordinator will get to know a child in both school and at home and any other setting to share strategies and provide resources to enable a consistent approach.
They will also liaise with other professionals such as social care, CAMHS, health professionals and any other agencies that may be involved with a child. Our home school co-ordinator holds Family Information sessions each half-term on topics that are of interest to parents and families. Maple Ridge will also signpost parents/carers to other organisations or services that provide additional support.
Our Home/School Coordinator is Mrs J Eales.
Coffee Morning and Task Force
Jane Eales holds a meet every Thursday morning, from 9.30-12pm.
Come along for Tea, Coffee, biscuits, and a chance to chat to other parents.
Some of our parents also volunteer to laminate, cut and stick visual symbols, and work tasks for our children to support their communication and learning.
So, if you would like to join us on a Thursday, for a cuppa and chat, or to help with making resources, you would be very welcome.
Hampshire Parent Carer Network (HPCN) :
HPCN offers parents and carers of children and young people aged 0-25 with any additional needs, or disability, including mental health (diagnosed or undiagnosed) the opportunity to tell the Local Authority, Health and other services, what life is really like.
They use their lived-in experience to shape, challenge and ultimately improve services for our children and young people living in Hampshire. Professionals have a duty to listen to parents and carers and with HPCN your voice will be heard loud and clear.
Email participation@hpcn.org.uk.
